1.0.0.en: 1 Adam, Sheth, Enosh, 2 Kenan, Mahalaleel, Jered, 3 Henoch, Methuselah, Lamech, 4 Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

1.0.2.en: Although the main or only source for this period is the Book of Genesis, the genealogies here are distinguished by highlighting and affirming two important elements: the divine election of the people of God, and the rootedness of divine grace in the presentation of the genealogies.

1.0.3.en: The line of genealogies runs here to serve the general purpose of the book, which is that God chooses for Himself a holy people: the literal Israel of the Old Testament, and the new Israel, that is, the Church, which gathers its members from all the nations.

1.0.4.en: Adam: a Hebrew name, whose literal meaning is "red." Some think that the origin of the word is the Akkadian or Assyrian "adamu," that is, "to make" or "to produce," as though God created man so that he might enjoy happiness in work and production.

1.0.5.en: It is true that the two books were concerned to affirm the authenticity and purity of the people of Israel, in contrast to the Samaritans, who carry mixed blood of Jews and Gentiles. But at the same time, the book begins with Adam as the father of all mankind. For salvation has now been accomplished by the Son of David, who is presented to the whole world.

1.0.6.en: The purpose of the genealogy is not to present the complete line, but to affirm these two theological truths: 1. The privilege of the ancient people as a chosen people consecrated to God, who had its own message among all the nations and peoples, and who tried to isolate itself from the pagan gods by descending from the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. 2. The kingdom of the Son of David is universal, opening the door of salvation, hope and heavenly glory to all mankind. For in Christ "there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all" (Col 3:11).

1.0.7.en: We should not be surprised that Cain and his offspring (Gen 4:17-26) are ignored in these genealogies. The book refuses to indicate the existence of all the generations that came from Cain, just as it ignores the northern kingdom after its rebellion against the house of David, its failure to keep the divine Law, and its establishing of a worship according to its own human thought. For what concerns the book is the declaration of the divine covenant between God and those who are faithful in clinging to Him and having fellowship with Him.

1.0.8.en: It began with Adam, like one reviewing all the genealogies of mankind, but it excludes the genealogies of all the peoples that do not reach Israel, in order to declare that God has a plan and a choice for accomplishing the salvation of mankind through the Son of David, who is from Israel.

1.1.0.en: The Book of Chronicles does not fail to care for the call of Abraham and for the covenant He made with Moses, but what concerns it most is the Temple and the covenant with David, as though what chiefly concerns the writer is the Promised Land and the unity of the people, whatever the cost[13], so that he may carry us across to the Son of David and the enjoyment of the heavenly Jerusalem.

1.1.1.en: Once again we affirm that the purpose of these genealogies is to present the line between Adam and Abraham: Adam as the common father of mankind, who was created in the image and likeness of God; and Abraham, who became the father of mankind in faith, who saw the Lord incarnate, crucified and risen from the dead, to raise up all peoples, and rejoiced and was glad (Jn 8:56).

1.1.2.en: v From the beginning, when the Lord created Adam, He made him a priest to stand in His service.

1.1.3.en: In truth the Lord set a limit for Adam (saying): Eat, O Adam, of all the fruits that are in Paradise.

1.1.4.en: But do not draw near to the tree that is in the midst, and when you come near to it, you shall surely die.

1.1.5.en: The evil one envied Adam, who was made in the image of God, and he seized Eve, and she plucked the fruit and ate of the tree.

1.1.6.en: And she gave to Adam and he ate, and he transgressed the commandment, and death reigned over Adam as it was said.

1.1.7.en: Adam died, and behold, death crept into all the generations, and came and reached, like a plunderer, as far as Moses...

1.2.0.en: All the righteous and the just, the prophets and the kings, tasted the cup of Adam, who transgressed the commandment[14].

1.2.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh v From Adam, the man who was not to beget, our mother Eve came forth; how much more ought we to believe that the daughter of Eve bears a child without a man!

1.3.0.en: The virgin earth bore the first Adam, who was head over all the earth, and today the Virgin bore the second Adam, who was head over all the heavens![15]

1.3.1.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian Sheth (Seth): a Semitic name meaning "appointed" or "helper." He was born after the killing of Abel to be a helper and comforter to his parents. For just as the child needs his parents, who are full of love, tenderness and care, so the parents also need their son or daughter. The wise man says: "A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother" (Prov 10:1). "A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him" (Prov 17:25). "A foolish son is the calamity of his father" (Prov 19:13).

1.3.2.en: Concerning Seth, St. Mar Jacob of Serugh shares with our first parents Adam and Eve the bitterness of their souls after the killing of Abel, and touches the wonderful divine consolations that overflowed upon them with the birth of their son Seth. The secret of their consolation is not that God gave them a son in place of Abel and Cain, since they had seen death for the first time in their lives (Abel) and understood how the earthly body returns to the dust, while the second, Cain, was in great terror, fearing the beasts and trembling even at his own shadow. Rather, they beheld in Seth the surpassing love of God and the consolations of heaven, and they understood divine mysteries that lifted their two hearts as though to heaven.

1.3.3.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh pictures Seth as bearing a type of the Lord Christ, as he assaulted the foundations of sorrow and shattered them, and trod upon grief with his feet, so that it lost its authority. Seth removed the gloom from his parents, and became like the swift-moving hart, before whom the serpents flee, lest he strike them with his feet and kill them. There was no longer any place for gloom in the hearts of Adam and Eve, since he gave them a medicine that healed them. It is said: "And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth" (Gen 5:3). In this he was a type of the Son of God, who is one with the Father, of whom it is said: "Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high" (Heb 1:3). But how great is the difference between the type and the One it signifies.

1.3.4.en: v Adam begat in his likeness (Gen 5:3), and after his image; and what does this (likeness) mean, which Moses wrote with care, if it did not signify something he wished to show us? Why was it necessary to write of Seth that he resembles?

1.3.5.en: He recorded the tribes from Adam to his own time, and did not mention that so-and-so resembles such-and-such his father...

1.3.6.en: Consolation came to the house of Adam through the beautiful Seth, and by his birth they forgot their former afflictions.

1.3.7.en: The radiance of the mystery blazed from his countenance and gladdened them, for they had been sorrowful because of Abel...

1.3.8.en: They saw in him a glorious likeness and marveled at his splendor, and by that wonder they forgot the mourning in which they had been grieved.

1.3.9.en: Eve saw in him the likeness of her husband Adam, and when he was far away, it was as though he were not far, because he was before her.

1.3.10.en: She comforted Adam with the beauty of his son, and said to him: Come and behold your image, and put away your sorrow.

1.3.11.en: Come, behold yourself and be comforted by your likeness, and look at your person, behold, he bears your image, he is wholly you.

1.3.12.en: Come, O tree, behold your fruit, for it is like you; O lofty eagle, behold, the likenesses of you are upon your little fledglings.

1.3.13.en: Draw near, O mighty one, chief of the earth and father of the races, and behold your son; his leg is as high as your leg.

1.4.0.en: Look, O plowman, behold, the seed of your field resembles you, and the bouquet you gathered is like you in all its beauty[16].

1.4.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh Enosh (Gen 4:26): a Hebrew name meaning "man." He was the first to teach mankind to praise God, for it is said: "And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD" (Gen 4:26).

1.4.2.en: v Enosh strove in his generation like one distinguished, and began and called upon the name of the Lord so that he might praise.

1.4.3.en: He distinguished and taught praise to the sons of his generation by his melody, that they might call upon the name of the Lord at all times.

1.4.4.en: His love boiled over with love for his Lord with discernment, and he gave the praises in righteousness at appointed times.

1.4.5.en: He appointed every morning and the evenings to call on the name of God, that he might weave his life upon spiritual benefits.

1.5.0.en: He opened the mouth of the earth and taught it to call upon the name of the Lord on all the days and nights[17].

1.7.0.en: Kenan[18]: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning owner, or possessor, or acquisition, or smith (forgeman).

1.7.1.en: Two bore the same name in the Old Testament: 1. Some think he was the fourth Patriarch of the fathers before the Flood, the firstborn of Enosh. At his birth Enosh was ninety years old; Kenan lived 70 years when Mahalaleel was born, lived 840 years after that, and died at the age of 910 years (Gen 5:9-14).

1.7.2.en: According to rabbinical tradition, he was the first to introduce the worship of idols and astrology.

1.8.0.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian affirms that the Chaldeans in the time of Terah and Abram his son worshipped the idol-god Kenan. Some think that his daughters were the first to make musical instruments and play on them[19]. 2. The son of Arphaxad and father of Shelah (Lk 3:35-36). He is usually called Kenan the second.

1.9.0.en: Mahalaleel (Gen 5:12-13): a Hebrew name meaning "praise of God." Two persons are found with this name: 1. The son of Kenan and grandson of Seth. At his birth his father was seventy years old; he begot Jared at the age of sixty-five, and lived until he reached 865 years (Gen 5:12-17; Lk 3:37). Ewald thinks that Mahalaleel knew the sun-god, and his son Jared knew the water-god, the Indian god Varune[20]. 2. A man of Judah, of the sons of Perez, of the descendants of Athaiah (Neh 11:4), who dwelt in Jerusalem after the captivity.

1.9.1.en: Jered (Gen 5:15-20): a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "descent," the father of Enoch.

1.10.0.en: Two are found bearing this name: 1. The son of Mahalaleel and father of Enoch; he was 162 years old at the birth of his son Enoch (Gen 5:15-20; Lk 3:37). 2. The son of Ezrah of the tribe of Judah, whose wife was a Jewess, Jehudiyah, the father of Gedor (1 Chr 4:18). The rabbis give a symbolic interpretation of his name, whose meaning is "descent," seeing in it that he bears the title "Moses-Jered," because Moses caused the descent of the manna[21].

1.11.1.en: Enoch: the Hebrew name "Hanoch," whose meaning is perhaps "initiated" or consecrated.

1.11.2.en: It is said in the Book of Genesis: "And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: and Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: and Methuselah lived an hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech. And Methuselah lived after he begat Lamech seven hundred eighty and two years, and begat sons and daughters: and all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died" (Gen 5:21-22, 25-27).

1.11.3.en: It is said of Enoch: "And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: and all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: and Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him" (Gen 5:22-24). St. Cyprian sees in Enoch a living example of those who are quickly translated to the Lord, because they left behind them the love of temporal things and clung to the heavenly.

1.12.0.en: v You will have pleased God (like Enoch) if you are found worthy of being removed from the contagion of the world. The Holy Spirit taught Solomon that those who please God are taken early and are quickly set free, lest by being delayed in this world they be defiled by its pestilence. As it is said: [He was snatched away lest evil should change his mind, for he was pleasing to God, and He loved him, and as he was living among sinners He translated him] (Wis 4:10-11). And in the Psalms, the soul that honors its God hastens toward Him, saying: "How amiable are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts! My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the LORD" (Ps 84:1-2)[22].

1.12.1.en: St. Cyprian v Enoch stood firm in a lofty and divine beauty, and purified his soul with holiness and purity.

1.12.2.en: He excelled in a radiant and pure way of life, and pleased God with thoughts full of love.

1.12.3.en: He was brought up with chaste and pure thoughts, and lived in purity without anxiety or anger.

1.12.4.en: And he dwelt in the wilderness without worldly movements, and pleased God three hundred years while He looked upon him.

1.12.5.en: He never found in him a fault, whether in his sleep or in his waking, nor a slack thought drawn toward the world.

1.13.0.en: He continued to look upon the Lord every day for three hundred years, and abode in His beauty, and was not stained by imperfections[23].

1.13.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh v Good are the wings of love, the true wings that flutter over the mouths of the Apostles; wings of fire that utter pure speech (Ps 12:6).

1.14.0.en: On those wings Enoch flew, when he was caught up to heaven (Gen 5:24)[24].

1.15.0.en: St. Ambrose v Some say that Adam, while looking at Enoch, was translated by God into Paradise, lest Adam think that Enoch had been killed like Abel and grieve. This happened so that Adam might also find rest concerning this righteous son of his, and so that he might know that for all who are like him, Paradise will be the fitting place for them, whether before death or after the resurrection[25].

1.15.1.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian Methuselah: a Semitic name meaning "man of the dart," the son of Enoch. He died in the year of the Flood at the age of 969 years, the longest life mentioned in the Holy Bible. But however long his life, it ended in death. It is said of him: "And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died" (Gen 5:27).

1.15.2.en: v Methuselah lived a little less than 1000 years, and he looked forward to the Son who makes men heirs of a life that has no end!

1.16.0.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian v Even if we lived nine hundred years or more, as men did before the Flood, and even if the days of Methuselah were granted to us, yet this span of long time, when it passes and ends, is counted as nothing. For whether a man lives ten years or a thousand years, when life ends and inevitable death comes, the past, long or short, is reckoned as one; except that he who lived longer is burdened with more sins, which he carries with him[26].

1.16.1.en: St. Jerome Lamech: St. Jerome sees that Lamech (Gen 4) did not have one wife, but was the first to marry two women, an allusion to the work of the heretics who divide the Church into churches that deviate from the faith. In any case, if Cain presented the most hideous example of crime at the beginning of human history by killing his brother unjustly, the fruit of evil is heresy, which corrupts the Church of God and distorts the faith.

1.17.0.en: v Lamech looked forward to Him (to the Lord Christ) to come, that He might grant him in love rest from his toil and the labor of his hands, and from the ground which the just God cursed (Gen 29:5)![27]

1.18.1.en: Noah (Gen 6): St. Ephrem the Syrian sees that Noah was a perfect righteous man in his generation, and that his three sons followed his example.

1.19.0.en: v Noah was a perfect man, and his three sons Shem, Ham and Japheth followed his example. Therefore each of them had only one wife, despite the great amount of fornication they saw. They followed their father's example, and held fast to the law of God which is in them by nature from the beginning of creation. For when He created Adam, He created with him only one woman... When the law departs from this, so that a male has several females or a female several males, that is injustice and wrong in nature[28].

1.19.1.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian God revealed to His righteous servant what He was about to do, for He said to him: "The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth" (Gen 6:13).

1.19.2.en: God could have commanded Noah to make the ark, and he would have obeyed in faith and trust. But God, as One who loves mankind, does not desire to be the One who gives commands and prohibitions, but the loving Friend who converses with man and reveals to him His plan, His wisdom and His secrets. As the psalmist says: "The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant" (Ps 25:14). He revealed to him that although He would destroy them with the earth, the destruction is the natural fruit of a corruption that they chose. This is seen from His saying: "The end of all flesh is come before me," as though He were saying: I did not wish this, but they made for themselves a destruction that brings their end; they chose it of their own free will. Now if the wicked have done this to themselves, bringing destruction even upon the earth, God does not leave His children to perish with them. Therefore He gave Noah a command to make an ark for his salvation, and the Holy Bible has presented to us the story of the ark with great precision and in some detail, because of the symbolic work the ark carried, which touches our salvation by the Cross.

1.20.0.en: When Noah was born, Lamech his father prophesied concerning him: "This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the LORD hath cursed" (Gen 5:29). Origen sees that this prophecy does not concern the old Noah, but the new Noah, who is Jesus Christ. For Noah means rest (that is, repose or comfort) and righteousness. He says: [Jesus alone gives rest to mankind, and frees the earth from the curse with which the Lord God cursed it[29].]

1.21.0.en: v In the Flood, in the days of Noah, all flesh died, but righteous Noah was preserved with his family... For the outward man perishes, but the inward is renewed. This happens not only in Baptism, but also by repentance, where the (lusts of the) flesh perish and the spirit grows, as the apostolic authority teaches us when he says: "I have judged already, as though I were present, concerning him that hath so done this deed... To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus" (1 Cor 5:3, 5)[30].

1.21.1.en: St. Ambrose v Yes, the ark that preserved living creatures, as a type, looked forward to our Lord who builds the holy Church, in which souls find a refuge...

1.22.0.en: The earth that was drowned by the Flood cried in silence to its Lord, and He came down and opened Baptism, by which men are drawn up to heaven![31]

1.23.0.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian Japheth: a Semitic name meaning "may he be spacious or wide[32]."

1.23.1.en: St. Jerome saw in the story of Noah, when he became drunk and uncovered himself, a symbolic picture of the Lord Christ, who drank the cup of suffering and for our sake was stripped on the Cross, and was mocked by the wicked, who are represented by Ham, while the Gentiles, symbolized by both Shem and Japheth, believed in Him. For he says:

1.23.2.en: [All this was said as a type of the Savior, who drank suffering on the Cross, saying: "O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me" (Mt 26:39). He drank and became drunk and His body was uncovered... For (Ham), that is, the Jews, came and laughed, but the younger, that is, the Gentiles, covered Him...

1.24.0.en: And as the father (Noah) was drunk with his sufferings, so the saints are drunk with the fragrance of their faith, they are drunk with the Holy Spirit. For yesterday you were gathering gold, and now you cast it from you; is this not counted drunkenness in the eyes of one who does not understand these things?! Finally, when the Holy Spirit descended on the disciples and filled them and they spoke in many tongues, they were accused of being drunk with new wine[33].]

1.25.0.en: v The two brothers (Shem and Japheth) who covered Noah (Gen 23:9) looked forward to the only Son who comes and covers the nakedness of Adam, whom pride had made drunk! The blessed Shem and Japheth looked forward to the blessed Son, who comes and frees Canaan from the slavery of sin![34]

1.26.s.en: B. Genealogies of the three sons of Noah

1.26.0.en: 5 The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras. 6 And the sons of Gomer; Ashchenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah. 7 And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim. 8 The sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, Put, and Canaan. 9 And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabta, and Raamah, and Sabtecha. And the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan. 10 And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be mighty upon the earth. 11 And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim, 12 And Pathrusim, and Casluhim, (of whom came the Philistines,) and Caphthorim. 13 And Canaan begat Zidon his firstborn, and Heth, 14 The Jebusite also, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite, 15 And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite, 16 And the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite. 17 The sons of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram, and Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Meshech. 18 And Arphaxad begat Shelah, and Shelah begat Eber. 19 And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg; because in his days the earth was divided: and his brother's name was Joktan. 20 And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah, 21 Hadoram also, and Uzal, and Diklah, 22 And Ebal, and Abimael, and Sheba, 23 And Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.

1.26.1.en: The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras. [5]

1.26.2.en: He began with the sons of Japheth, who were born in the region of the West, in the cities of Europe, and of whom he did not speak much [5-7], because the Jews at that time had rare dealings with them, and perhaps had no relation with them at all.

1.26.3.en: Gomer: perhaps its meaning is "the end of perfection," especially the perfection of failure, and the wife of the prophet Hosea bore the same name: "Gomer the daughter of Diblaim" (Hos 1:3).

1.26.4.en: It is observed that the sons of Japheth were mentioned first, then the sons of Ham, and finally the sons of Shem, who is the only one whose line is completed and leads to Abraham. Then the offspring of Abraham is recorded: Ishmael and his sons, likewise the sons of Abraham by Keturah, and finally Isaac the son of Abraham; then the offspring of Isaac follows, beginning with the offspring of Esau, but the line that leads to the Lord Christ continues through Jacob the son of Isaac.

1.26.5.en: Gomer is the son of Japheth the son of Noah (Gen 10:2-3), and the father of Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah. It is probable that from them came the tribes that the Assyrians called "Gimirrai" and the Greeks "Cimmerians."

1.27.0.en: The descendants of Gomer dwelt in the north; Homer the Greek called them "the people of the farthest north[35]," and Herodotus mentioned that they came in the seventh century B.C. into Asia from the regions beyond the Caucasus[36], and settled in Cappadocia, and threatened the Assyrian Empire, but Esarhaddon defeated them. As they turned toward the west they occupied Asia Minor and fought more than one battle with Gyges, king of Lydia, which ended in his being killed, and perhaps he is the one called in the Holy Bible by the name Gog[37]. After that they were driven out of Asia (Lydia) by Alyattes[38].

1.27.1.en: Magog: a Hebrew word meaning "the land of Gog" (Gen 10:2). Some think that "ma" is of Coptic origin and means "land." The name Magog became joined to the name Gog, and the two names became a symbol of resistance to the Christian faith (Rev 20:7-9).

1.27.2.en: In the Middle Ages the Syrians called the land of the Tartars Magog, while the Arabs called the land lying between the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea Magog, but the majority reckoned the Scythians to be the people of Magog. Herodotus describes them as a savage people who never washed with water, who drink the blood of the first enemy they kill, and use the scalps of their enemies as handkerchiefs or towels, and skulls as cups from which they drink, and offer the last captive of every hundred as a sacrifice to their gods, and among the gods they worship is the drawn sword. The Apostle Paul referred to them as an example of savagery (Col 3:11).

1.27.3.en: Tubal and Meshech: the two are often mentioned together (Gen 10:2); the two peoples were traders in slaves and bronze in the markets of Phoenicia (Ezek 27:13). They were famous in ancient times as warriors (Ezek 32:26), and they are also mentioned in the armies of Gog (Ezek 38:2; 39:1).

1.27.4.en: Josephus thinks they were the Iberians (Hbrrians) and the Cappadocians, while some think they were the Tibareni and the Moschi, whom Herodotus mentioned as part of the nineteenth province of the kingdom of Darius.

1.28.0.en: Tiras: a Hebrew name meaning "fearful." The ancients, such as St. Jerome[39] and the historian Josephus[40], considered that his offspring were the Thracians. Some contemporary scholars think they were the Tyrsenians, who were famous for piracy in the Aegean Sea, and were related to the Etruscans, the inhabitants of Italy in the earliest ages.

1.29.0.en: And the sons of Gomer; Ashchenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah. [6]

1.29.1.en: Ashkenaz: a people was named after him, mentioned in (Jeremiah 51:27) together with Ararat and Minni, perhaps in the region of Ararat (Armenia). It seems that they are the Scythians who lived in the time of Jeremiah near Lake Urmia. The Jews of the Middle Ages gave the name Ashkenazim to the Jews of Eastern Europe, believing that Ashkenaz is Germany.

1.29.2.en: Togarmah (Gen 10:3): some think the name is derived from two words, "toka" meaning "tribe" and "arma" meaning Armenia. It was probably in the southeast of Armenia. It was famous for horses, horsemen and mules (Ezek 27:13-14).

1.30.0.en: And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim. [7]

1.30.1.en: Elishah: this name means "God saves" (Gen 10:4). It was applied to a certain region, which was a source from which the Tyrians obtained purple (Ezek 27:7). It appears from (Genesis 10:4-5) that his descendants were among the Greeks who settled in the islands and on the coasts of the Mediterranean.

1.30.2.en: Tarshish: the name "Tarshish" means in Hebrew "chrysolite." Some think it is a Phoenician word meaning "a refinery," and some suppose that Tarshish was the ancestor of the peoples of the Mediterranean.

1.30.3.en: There is a city of Tarshish, which is Tartessus in southern Spain, near Gibraltar. Perhaps Tartessus is Carthage, the city lying in North Africa. When St. Augustine reached the age of sixteen, his father wanted to send him to Carthage to become skilled in eloquence.

1.30.4.en: Some suppose that the name Tarshish carries the meaning of mining or smelting metals, and could be applied to any land that has metal mines.

1.30.5.en: Some think that the "ships of Tarshish" are not connected with a particular place, but denote a particular kind of ship distinguished by its magnificence and its ability to sail on the high seas.

1.30.6.en: Kittim: some of the names in the genealogies belong to peoples that sprang from persons, and the name of the people or region or city was often derived from the name of the person.

1.30.7.en: It is probable that Kittim (Gen 10:4) is Cyprus. Some think it was a name applied to the islands and the shores west of Palestine. It was also applied to Macedonia in the age of the Maccabees (1 Macc 1:1).

1.31.0.en: The sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, Put, and Canaan. [8]

1.31.1.en: After the sons of Japheth, he spoke of those who bore a kind of enmity toward the Jews (the Church of the Old Testament), such as the sons of Ham, who went southward into Africa and also toward Asia. For the attention was centered on the Jews of the descendants of Shem, from whom Christ comes incarnate for the salvation of all the nations. On the one hand it is said: "I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee" (Isa 43:3). At the same time it is said: "Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?" (Mal 2:10). So if He seemed to favor the Jews for a time, that was to prepare for the incarnation of the Word of God from the seed of David for the salvation of the world. For all mankind is of the seed of Adam, and after the Flood of the seed of Noah. So all are called to sonship to God, as He is one Father of all (Eph 4:6); "But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand" (Isa 64:8).

1.32.0.en: The names of places or tribes are mentioned as though they were persons. So it is said here: "The sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, Put, and Canaan" (1 Chr 1:8). What is meant is that the sons of Ham are the Egyptians and the Canaanites, and so on. For the expression "son of..." or "sons of..." in Semitic has a wider meaning than a person born of a person[41].

1.32.1.en: The offspring of Ham presented, in general, peoples and nations resistant to the work of God and to His people in the Old Testament, so the Old Testament proclaims divine punishment upon these peoples, as they bear symbols of evil. Cush sometimes signified the darkness of ignorance, Egypt the love of the world that enslaves the soul, Canaan the work of Satan, and so on. But the prophecies of the Old Testament did not leave these peoples without hope; rather they announced the rejection of the faith by the people of God and the entry of these nations into the divine covenant. Thus the nations that were under the curse because of their idolatry, their resistance to faith in God and their abominations, became the holy Bride preparing for eternal life in the bosom of the heavenly Father.

1.33.0.en: Cush: it means "black" in Hebrew. Cush, the firstborn of Ham, begot five sons who presented five peoples: Seba "man," Havilah "circle or district," Sabtah "striker," Raamah "trembling," Sabtechah "striker"[42]. These peoples dwelt in the middle of the Arabian land and its south at the Persian Gulf, but Seba migrated to Africa (Ethiopia); therefore Cush in the Old Testament means Ethiopia and Nubia (south of Egypt), and sometimes Yemen or the south and middle of the Arabian peninsula. In many Bible dictionaries Cush is considered to be only Ethiopia.

1.33.1.en: The Son of David came to reconcile heaven with earth, and a people with the peoples, so that the believers from the Gentiles might become brothers who know nothing but love and unity.

1.33.2.en: Mizraim: the word "Mizraim" in Hebrew is a dual, so some thought it was so called because of the existence of Lower Egypt and Upper Egypt, or because the River Nile divides it into an eastern bank and a western one; but the more likely opinion is that it was called "Misr" in Arabic from the Hebrew, after Mizraim, where he and his sons dwelt, although his offspring extended to neighboring lands.

1.33.3.en: Put: a people related or akin to the Egyptians (Gen 10:6), mentioned with Egypt and other African countries, especially Lubim (Nah 3:9), and Lud (Ezek 27:10), between Cush and Lud. In the Septuagint it appears as "Libyans," and Josephus considered it Libya. Libya was called Putu in the Babylonian inscriptions; perhaps it was Cyrenaica, the eastern part of present-day Libya.

1.34.0.en: Canaan: from his offspring appeared the Canaanite tribes, and we have spoken briefly about some of these tribes in the introduction to the Book of Joshua[43].

1.34.1.en: The Book of Joshua is also considered the book of the acceptance of the Gentiles. For although the people had to inherit Canaan after driving out the pagans, God does not reject them, but rejects their idolatry and their evil. And when Rahab the Canaanite harlot declared her faith, she and her family enjoyed salvation, and she had the honor, from which many Hebrew women were deprived, that from her offspring the Messiah the Savior would come. Her name was recorded in the genealogy of the Lord Christ (Mt 1:5), a thing from which many were deprived, even among the heroes of faith and the prophets! God does not reject a single human being, but seeks the salvation of all: "Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4).

1.35.0.en: And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabta, and Raamah, and Sabtecha.

1.35.1.en: And the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan. [9]

1.35.2.en: Raama or Raamah: a grandson of Ham. There was a district in the southwest of Arabia that traded with Tyre in spices, precious stones and gold (Ezek 27:22). It is thought that its inhabitants were descendants of Raamah.

1.35.3.en: Sheba and Dedan: the sons of Raamah of the sons of Cush (Gen 10:7). Some think that Sheba is the name of an Arabian tribe, so they are Semites. As for the saying that Sheba and Dedan are of the offspring of Cush, some of these Semitic tribes migrated to Ethiopia and mingled with the offspring of Cush, and some of their clans migrated to the north.

1.35.4.en: The name of Sheba and the names of some of his brothers, such as Hazarmaveth and Uzal (Sana'a), are still applied to parts of the south of the Arabian peninsula.

1.36.0.en: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be mighty upon the earth. [10]

1.37.0.en: Nimrod: if the Holy Bible has presented a revelation of His work through the offspring of Shem, where the Word of God comes incarnate from the offspring of Abraham, it also reveals the work of the enemy of good, especially through the offspring of Cush, who presented Nimrod, and from the offspring of Canaan, who presented the Canaanite peoples resisting the work of God. As for Nimrod the son of Cush, it is said: "Which began to be a mighty one in the earth. He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD" (Gen 10:8-9). He was a mighty hunter, and founded the ruling dynasty in Babylon, Shinar and Akkad, and perhaps he himself was Gilgamesh the Akkadian or Babylonian. In any case, Babylon later became a symbol of rebellion against God and of pride, as also of spiritual fornication (Rev 14:8; 16:19; 17:1-5). Babylon came to signify the company of the wicked, and as St. Augustine says[44]: [as to the kingdom of the Antichrist[45].]

1.38.0.en: It is said of Nimrod, "He was a mighty hunter before the LORD" (Gen 10:9), and the saints Augustine and Mar Ephrem the Syrian see that it means he was a mighty hunter against the Lord God[46].

1.39.0.en: v He (Nimrod) pointed to Satan, the mighty evil one. He said that the beginning of his kingdom is Babel. The interpretation of Babel is division (confusion). Is division not truly the beginning of the kingdom of the devil?[47]

1.40.0.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian However, St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian sees, on the other hand, that Nimrod, in his resistance to the other nations, was only fulfilling the will of God for them. Concerning Nimrod, Moses said: "He was a mighty hunter before the LORD" (Gen 10:9), because according to the will of the Lord he waged war against each of these nations and drove it out from there, so that they would leave their places and settle in the places God had prepared for them... When blessing a chief or ruler, one used to say: [May you be like Nimrod, a mighty hunter victorious in the battles of the Lord](*)[48].

1.41.0.en: St. John Chrysostom says that some see in the words "before the LORD" the meaning against the Lord, but he sees the opposite: [Rather it shows that (Nimrod) was strong and brave. For the expression "before the LORD" means he was created by Him. And perhaps it means that God makes us marvel at him, since He created a wonderful creature, and sets him before us on the earth[49].]

1.42.0.en: And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim, [11]

1.43.0.en: Ludim: from him came the people of Lud or the Ludites, who are different from the people of Lud of the offspring of Shem [22]. These are of the offspring of Mizraim; they used to dwell west of the Nile toward Libya.

1.43.1.en: Anamim: it seems that the tribe of his offspring dwelt in Libya.

1.43.2.en: Lehabim: it seems that the tribe of Lehabim is the very tribe of Lubim or "the Libyans," who are Africans, originating in Egypt.

1.43.3.en: Naphtuhim: his offspring were of the inhabitants of Middle Egypt, near Memphis, the center of the god Ptah, and perhaps some of them migrated to Ethiopia.

1.44.0.en: And Pathrusim, and Casluhim, (of whom came the Philistines,) and Caphthorim. [12]

1.44.1.en: Pathrusim: they dwelt in Pathros in Upper Egypt. The word "Pathros" means "the land of the south."

1.44.2.en: Casluhim: its meaning is "fortified"; his offspring most probably dwelt in "Kasiyus," a mountainous region east of Balsam, on the border of Egypt on the side of Palestine.

1.44.3.en: From Casluhim came the Philistines, whose offspring migrated to Palestine, and there the ancient Philistine people arose. Perhaps the word Palestine is derived from "Philistim," and it means "an emigrant" or "a migrant."

1.44.4.en: The Philistines were constant enemies of the children of Israel from the days of the judges; David weakened their power (1 Sam 4:1). They settled on the western side of Canaan along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea; they surpassed Israel in number and in military skill, and knew the secret of making weapons of iron (1 Sam 13:19-22).

1.44.5.en: From Casluhim also came Caphtorim, which means "crowns"; his offspring dwelt in Caphtor, which some suppose was in Cappadocia in Asia Minor, and others think it was Cyprus or the island of Crete, while still others think it was in the Delta of Egypt near Memphis, where there was a city called "Kabt-hor," which is likely "Caphtor."

1.45.0.en: And Canaan begat Zidon his firstborn, and Heth, [13]

1.46.0.en: Canaan: the youngest son of Ham, from whose offspring the Canaanite tribes appeared, and we have spoken briefly about some of these tribes in the introduction to the Book of Joshua[50].

1.46.1.en: Canaan was the great-grandfather of the Canaanites, who plunged deeply into evil, and who were divided into many nations: the Hittites, the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites, and so on. The children of Israel took possession of the region under the leadership of Joshua the son of Nun, and it was called the Promised Land. Origen sees that the driving out of these nations signifies the driving out of sins and getting rid of them, so that the believer may enjoy the Kingdom of God within him under the leadership of the Lord of glory Jesus, through divine grace.

1.46.2.en: Zidon or Sidon: a Semitic name meaning "a place of fishing." An ancient, wealthy Phoenician port, extending along a coast about two miles wide between the mountains of Lebanon and the Mediterranean, 22 miles north of Tyre. Its name is taken from Zidon, the firstborn of Canaan the son of Ham the son of Noah.

1.46.3.en: It exported carved ivory, gold, silver, ornaments and glass vessels. It governed itself. The children of Israel failed to take possession of it, and the Sidonians harassed them in the days of the judges. The two civilizations interacted, and the Israelites worshipped the gods of Sidon, among them Baal and Ashtaroth.

1.46.4.en: When Ahab married Jezebel, the daughter of one of the kings of Sidon and the chief priest of Baal there, she spread the worship of Baal in Israel, and made every effort to wipe out the worship of the living God.

1.46.5.en: Sidon fell before Assyria, and consequently was subject to Babylon and Persia, then to the Greeks and the Romans. And in the days of the Lord Christ many of them were Greeks, who went to Galilee to hear the Lord Christ and to meet with Him.

1.47.0.en: The Jebusite also, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite, [14]

1.47.1.en: The names mentioned in these verses [14-17] do not belong to persons but to peoples, all of which sprang from Canaan. The names of peoples were used instead of the names of the persons who established these peoples, to affirm that the human race, which arose through one man "Adam," turned into many peoples and nations. And the genealogy ends in looking forward to the coming of the Lord Christ, who gathers the believers from all the world, so that they become like a great and beautiful building. So the Asian meets with the African and with the European, and so on, in the Son of David, and the King of kings sits in the heart of His people, establishing His joyful Kingdom which includes all. Then it is said: "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus" (Gal 3:28)[51].

1.47.2.en: The Girgashite or Girgashites: the Girgashite is mentioned among the tribes of the Canaanites in the Table of Nations (Gen 10:16), and they are also mentioned among the Canaanite tribes whose land the Lord promised to give as an inheritance to the children of Israel (Gen 15:21; Deut 7:1; Josh 3:10; 24:11).

1.47.3.en: Some think it probable that they are the "sons of Grgs," whose name appears in the Ugarit texts of the thirteenth century B.C.

1.48.0.en: And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite, [15]

1.48.1.en: The Hivites: some of them dwelt in Shechem, whose ruler was Hamor the Hivite in the days of Jacob (Gen 33:19; 34:2).

1.48.2.en: They dwelt in parts of Syria and Palestine, and were mentioned with the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Jebusites and the Girgashites (Ex 3:8; 23:28; Deut 7:1).

1.48.3.en: Since deviation to idol worship and the practice of pagan abominations was attractive to many of the believers at that time, the commandment came strict and firm not to cling to these peoples, and yet in spite of all this even Solomon the wise himself fell into it. The commandment came explicit, suited to that age literally: "When the LORD thy God shall bring thee into the land whither thou goest to possess it, and hath cast out many nations before thee, the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than thou; and when the LORD thy God shall deliver them before thee; thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them" (Deut 7:1-2). The purpose of this commandment is to create a pure Church, a holy family, and a kingdom justified in the Lord, preserved from pagan abominations.

1.48.4.en: We often err in evaluating what is recorded in the Old Testament from an unsound viewpoint, ignoring the language of the time. For the circumstances surrounding the people at that time were completely different from what we live today in the age of grace, and their concepts are not our concepts. For this reason they needed a commandment to support their salvation. These severe commands are understood in our life as symbols:

1.48.5.en: a. Not making a covenant with them means our refusal to be lenient with sin, and to open the door of dialogue with it.

1.48.6.en: b. Not intermarrying with them (Deut 7:3), for there is no fellowship between the believer and the unbeliever in married life, nor between light and darkness. For the believer's acceptance of union with the unbeliever at the level of family relationships comes about at the expense of the salvation of the soul and the sanctification of the family.
